specification.problem: Realise a single-qubit generalised measurement (POVM) on a photon-polarisation qubit by means of a discrete-time quantum walk in which the position (optical path) register is expanded through polarisation-dependent translations and position-dependent coin (polarisation) rotations, and the POVM outcome is read out from the final position of the photon.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful construction (chosen because no experiment_scope was supplied): the 3-outcome Trine-POVM on one qubit, implemented by a 3-step quantum walk on three positions x in {0,1,2} with an asymmetric polarisation-dependent shift (beam-displacer model) and explicit site-dependent coins. The SIC-POVM (4 outcomes), the unambiguous state discrimination scheme, and all experimental details (wave-plate angles, beam-displacer geometry, detector calibration, imperfections) are outside this scope.

symbols.meaning: Horizontal and vertical polarisation basis states of the photon, identified with the computational basis |0\rangle, |1\rangle of the coin qubit
Position (optical path) basis state of the walker
Unknown input polarisation qubit state to be measured
Density operator of the input qubit (allows mixed states)

symbols.meaning: Trine states, three pure states with Bloch vectors uniformly spaced (120 degrees apart) on a great circle
POVM element associated with outcome k (detection at position x=k)

symbols.meaning: Kraus operator (on the coin space) mapping the initial coin state to the unnormalised coin state found at final position x
symbols.domain: 2x2 complex matrices with \sum_x K_x^\dagger K_x = I

Polarisation-dependent shift (translation) operator realised by a birefringent beam displacer

equations.label: Trine POVM
equations.description: Three rank-one POVM elements whose Bloch vectors \vec n_k = (\sin(2k\pi/3), 0, \cos(2k\pi/3)) are uniformly distributed on a great circle (here the x-z plane) of the Bloch sphere; the weight 2/3 enforces completeness.
equations.abstract_quote: Trine-POVM, i.e., the POVM elements uniformly distributed on an equatorial plane of the Bloch sphere
equations.justification: The abstract defines the trine as POVM elements uniformly distributed on an equatorial plane; three equally weighted rank-one elements at 120-degree Bloch spacing is the standard mathematical content of that statement. The specific plane (x-z, real amplitudes) and phase convention are chosen here.
assumptions: The great circle is taken to be the x-z plane with |\psi_0\rangle = |H\rangle; any other equatorial plane is related by a fixed polarisation unitary.
Rank-one elements with equal weights 2/3 are assumed (the minimal informationally symmetric trine).

equations.label: Quantum-walk step with polarisation-dependent translation
equations.latex: U_t = S\,\Big(\sum_{x} C^{(t)}_x \otimes |x\rangle\langle x|\Big),\qquad S = |H\rangle\langle H| \otimes \sum_x |x\rangle\langle x| + |V\rangle\langle V| \otimes \sum_x |x+1\rangle\langle x|
equations.description: One step of the walk: a position-dependent coin acts on the polarisation, then the shift leaves H-polarised amplitude in place and displaces V-polarised amplitude by one position (beam-displacer model).
equations.abstract_quote: the polarisation-dependent translation is performed via birefringent beam displacers and a change of the polarisation is implemented with the help of wave-plates
equations.justification: The abstract states that the walk consists of polarisation-dependent translations (beam displacers) and polarisation changes (wave-plates); the operator form is the standard quantum-walk decomposition into coin and conditional shift. The asymmetric (one polarisation displaced, the other transmitted) form models a birefringent beam displacer.
assumptions: Asymmetric shift (H stays, V moves by +1) rather than the symmetric ±1 shift; the two are equivalent up to relabelling of positions.
Coins may depend on both position and step number (different wave-plates in different paths).

equations.label: POVM induced by position readout
equations.latex: K_x = (I \otimes \langle x|)\,U_3 U_2 U_1\,(I \otimes |0\rangle),\qquad E_x = K_x^\dagger K_x,\qquad p_x = \mathrm{Tr}(E_x \rho) = \sum_{c\in\{H,V\}} \big|\langle c, x|\,U_3U_2U_1\,|\psi,0\rangle\big|^2
equations.description: Starting the walker at position 0 and detecting its final position x (without resolving polarisation) implements a POVM on the coin qubit whose elements are determined by the Kraus operators K_x; completeness \sum_x E_x = I follows from unitarity.
equations.justification: Standard Naimark-dilation reading of a quantum walk as a generalised measurement on the coin: the position register is the ancilla, the walk is the dilating unitary, and position detection is the projective readout.
assumptions: Three walk steps are sufficient for the trine (true for the construction in eq_4).
Detectors resolve position only; polarisation at the detector is traced out.

equations.label: Explicit coin schedule for the trine walk (proposed instance)
equations.latex: C^{(1)}_0 = I,\quad C^{(2)}_0 = \begin{pmatrix} \sqrt{2/3} & -\sqrt{1/3} \\ \sqrt{1/3} & \sqrt{2/3} \end{pmatrix},\quad C^{(2)}_1 = \sigma_x,\quad C^{(3)}_0 = I,\quad C^{(3)}_1 = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt 2}\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 \end{pmatrix},\quad C^{(3)}_2 = I
equations.description: Step 1 only separates H (x=0) from V (x=1). Step 2 peels off the first POVM element at x=0 with a rotation of amplitude \sqrt{2/3}, sends the remaining amplitude to x=1, and flips polarisation at x=1 so that the two contributions merge at x=1. Step 3 applies a Hadamard at x=1 followed by the shift, splitting the merged state into outcomes x=1 (H) and x=2 (V).
equations.justification: A concrete coin schedule constructed here so that eq_3 reproduces eq_1; it is not taken from the abstract, which gives no coin parameters.
assumptions: Matrices written in the ordered basis (|H\rangle, |V\rangle).
Coins at unoccupied positions are irrelevant and set to I.
Mapping of these coins to physical wave-plate angles is not specified.

equations.label: Resulting Kraus operators and POVM elements
equations.latex: K_0 = \sqrt{\tfrac{2}{3}}\,|H\rangle\langle H|,\qquad K_1 = \sqrt{\tfrac{2}{3}}\,|H\rangle\langle\psi_1|,\qquad K_2 = -\sqrt{\tfrac{2}{3}}\,|V\rangle\langle\psi_2|,\qquad K_x^\dagger K_x = \tfrac{2}{3}|\psi_x\rangle\langle\psi_x| = E_x
equations.description: Applying eq_3 to the schedule of eq_4 yields rank-one Kraus operators whose squares are exactly the trine elements of eq_1; the equality is exact (no approximation).
equations.justification: Direct algebraic consequence of eq_2-eq_4: after step 2 the coin state at x=1 is M|\psi\rangle with M = |H\rangle\langle V| + 3^{-1/2}|V\rangle\langle H|, and M^\dagger|\pm\rangle \propto |\psi_{1,2}\rangle with squared norm 2/3. Not verified numerically here.
assumptions: Ideal lossless optics and perfect interference of the two paths merging at x=1 (interferometric phase stability).

equations.label: Outcome statistics in Bloch form
equations.description: Probability of detecting the photon at position k as a function of the input Bloch vector; the three probabilities determine the two Bloch components lying in the trine plane.
equations.justification: Born rule for rank-one POVM elements written in Bloch-vector form; standard for the trine measurement.
assumptions: Trine plane and labelling as in eq_1.

registers.name: position (optical path)
registers.size: 3 levels (2 qubits if binary-encoded, x = 2 x_1 + x_0)
registers.role: Ancilla / walker position; the final position x in {0,1,2} is the POVM outcome label

specification.initial_state: |\Psi_0\rangle = |\psi\rangle \otimes |x=0\rangle = (\alpha|H\rangle + \beta|V\rangle)\otimes|0\rangle, with the position register on the top (x=0) path.

steps.description: Prepare the input polarisation state |\psi\rangle on a single photon in path x=0.
Walk step 1: identity coin, then polarisation-dependent shift S; H amplitude stays in x=0, V amplitude moves to x=1.

Walk step 2: apply coin C^{(2)}_0 (rotation with amplitude \sqrt{2/3} on H) at x=0 and \sigma_x at x=1, then shift S; the H part at x=0 becomes outcome 0, the V part of x=0 moves to x=1 and merges with the flipped amplitude already at x=1.
Walk step 3: apply the Hadamard coin at x=1 (identity at x=0), then shift S; H output stays at x=1 (outcome 1), V output moves to x=2 (outcome 2).
Detect the photon's final position x in {0,1,2}, which realises the trine POVM with elements E_x.

specification.measurement: Single-photon detection in each of the three output paths x = 0, 1, 2 (position basis of the walker), without resolving polarisation. Outcome k corresponds to the POVM element E_k = (2/3)|\psi_k\rangle\langle\psi_k|.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Estimate p_k from detection frequencies over many repetitions; compare with eq_6 (p_k = (1 + \vec r\cdot\vec n_k)/3), optionally inverting to estimate the two in-plane Bloch components of the input state. Check \sum_k p_k = 1 (after loss normalisation).
assumptions: Scope choice: only the Trine-POVM is reconstructed; the SIC-POVM and the unambiguous-discrimination POVM named in the abstract are left outside this scope.
Trine plane fixed to the x-z Bloch plane with |\psi_0\rangle = |H\rangle (real amplitudes); other equatorial planes differ by a fixed polarisation unitary.
Beam displacer modelled as the asymmetric shift (H transmitted, V displaced by one position).
Coin schedule of eq_4 is a proposed construction, not extracted from the paper; the paper's actual coins/wave-plate settings may differ.
Ideal, lossless, phase-stable optics; position-only detection.
missing_information: The paper's actual quantum-walk layout (number of steps, positions, symmetric vs asymmetric shift) and its wave-plate angles for each coin.

Construction details for the SIC-POVM (4 outcomes, presumably more walk steps) and for the unambiguous discrimination POVM (including the inconclusive outcome and the pair of non-orthogonal states used).
Experimental figures of merit (fidelities, detection efficiencies, losses) and any error model.
Mapping of abstract coins to physical half-/quarter-wave-plate settings and the treatment of relative phases between merging paths.
